children: Javed Farooqui Mumbai: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has roped in non-banking financial company Muthoot FinCorp as the title sponsor for all international matches organised by the board till March 2028 for up to 150 crore, sources aware of the development told ET. Muthoot FinCorp's per-match payout is up to 4.3 crore, against the 4.85 crore sought by the BCCI for 35 matches in the current cycle, they added.

It is pertinent to note that IDFC First, the previous title sponsor, was paying 4.2 crore per match for the previous cycle involving 56 matches that ended in August. IDFC First had secured the rights in 2023 under a three-year agreement worth 235.2 crore. The BCCI had first floated the tender for the sale of title sponsorship rights on July 20, with August 13 being the last date to submit bids, which was later extended to September. "BCCI has done a direct deal with Muthoot FinCorp as it was unable to find a partner through the tender process," said one of the sources aware of the development.

A sports marketing official said the new deal, while higher than the 4.2 crore paid by IDFC First, is less than the 4.85 crore per-match base price set by the BCCI. "Clearly, the deal shows that the cricket sponsorship market continues to be resilient. However, it is also a reality check for the BCCI as it failed to meet its ambition," the official noted.

The new deal comes close on the heels of the BCCI roping in Campa, SBI Life and ChatGPT as associate partners for bilateral cricket involving Team India. The three new sponsorship deals had a combined value of over 130 crore, representing a 44% increase over the previous cycle. People familiar with the development had earlier told ET that Campa Cola emerged as the highest bidder at 1.31 crore per match, followed by ChatGPT and SBI Life at 1.2 crore each.

Bisleri and Indian Oil Corporation, both of which bid 1.2 crore per match, were also in the fray for associate partnerships. The BCCI had raised the reserve price for associate partner rights to 95 lakh per match from 82 lakh previously.

title: Muthoot FinCorp Bags BCCI Sponsorship Rights Till 2028
